bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Structural weakness in the German/European automotive end-market that the Metallurgy business depends on — The Board's Report says 'The Metallurgy segment continues to operate in a difficult European environment, impacted by weakness in the German automotive sector, elevated energy costs and broader geopolitical uncertainty', and that management states 'increased exposure to defence is necessary to reduce dependence on the weaker automotive industry and support future profitable growth' - i.e. the current customer base is itself the risk, and the pivot to defence and specialised engineering is unproven.
- Elevated energy costs and European cost competitiveness at the Eisenwerk Erla foundry — Elevated energy costs are named as a driver of the Metallurgy segment's difficulty alongside German automotive weakness and geopolitical uncertainty. Foundry and machining economics are energy-intensive, and the stated response is limited to 'very strict cost discipline, operational efficiency measures and a strategic shift toward higher-value applications', which does not remove the input-cost exposure.
- Execution risk on the UK restructuring and the transfer of manufacturing to Bangalore — UK Hydraulics revenue 'declined 25.5% due to product rationalisation and ongoing restructuring initiatives' and 'reduced OEM demand'. The Group states 'the returns from coordination and integrated operations between the Indian and UK operations having substantially diminished' and has completed a transfer of manufacturing capacity to Bangalore. The margin recovery is stated only as an expectation 'over the medium term', so revenue has already been lost while the benefit is still pending.
- Concentration on a small number of large global aerospace OEM programmes — Aerospace 'continued to be the primary growth driver' and growth is 'underpinned by long-term programmes with major OEMs including Airbus, Boeing, Bell Textron, Dassault Aviation and Deutsche Aircraft'. Segment revenue is therefore tied to a handful of OEM build rates and programme decisions the Company does not control, and the same OEM set also underwrites the 'new strategic partnerships' management says will support long-term visibility.
- Margin dilution from aerospace programme ramp-up and growth investment — The Board's Report notes that while 'revenue momentum remains robust, profitability was broadly stable and grew moderately during the year, indicating some margin normalization amid growth investments and project mix'. The company itself identifies 'disciplined programme ramp-up and long-term execution excellence as the keys to enhancing competitiveness, margins and return on capital employed' — an admission that a mis-managed ramp erodes returns.
- Raw material availability, commodity input costs and customer financing conditions — Explicitly flagged for the near term: 'Near-term performance will remain influenced by raw material availability, commodity input costs, and financing conditions for end customers.' The last of these adds a credit-cycle dependency on top of the Company's own input-cost exposure.
- Data privacy and cyber security across operations and the supply chain — Named a Risk in the BRSR material-issues table with negative financial implications: 'Inadequate safeguards may lead to data breaches, loss of stakeholder trust, and compliance issues.' Material for a defence and aerospace supplier handling OEM-controlled technical data; mitigation is an ISO 27001-aligned information security management system with risk assessments, firewalls, intrusion detection and endpoint protection.
- Workplace health, safety, human-rights and labour standards across a global manufacturing footprint — Two BRSR material issues rated Risk with negative implications. Failure to control workplace hazards 'can lead to accidents, regulatory non-compliance, and reputational damage', and labour-rights lapses 'may lead to legal penalties, reputational damage, lower ESG ratings and operational disruptions'. Heightened because the Company operates 'in sectors like aerospace and automotive manufacturing, where labour standards and safety are critical', and the stated risk explicitly extends beyond own operations to the 'global supply chain'.
- Water scarcity and environmental footprint at manufacturing sites — BRSR names water management a Risk: 'Water scarcity poses a risk to DTL by potentially disrupting manufacturing operations, Inadequate water management can lead to increased operational costs, regulatory challenges, and reputational concerns.' (punctuation as printed in the report).

business.body: Dynamatic Technologies Limited, incorporated in 1973 and listed on the BSE and NSE, describes itself as a manufacturing and engineering services company operating in two disclosed business activities - Aerospace & Defence and Hydraulics - which together account for 100% of turnover, with a third Metallurgy business run through its German subsidiary Eisenwerk Erla. Through Dynamatic-Oldland Aerospace it manufactures flight-critical airframe structures and high-precision Class 1 parts as a Tier-I supplier to Airbus, Boeing, Bell, Deutsche Aircraft, Dassault Aviation, Hutchinson and Thales, and domestically to defence PSUs HAL and BEL; typical work packages are control surfaces (wings, ailerons, wing flaps), fuselages, doors and flap track beams. outlook.body:
- Make Aerospace & Defence the centre of gravity of the Group - the Chairman calls it 'the primary engine of Dynamatic's revenues and profitability throughout FY 2025-26, consistently delivering superior margins' - by 'scaling complex aerostructure programs, deepening relationships with global OEMs and strengthening advanced manufacturing and engineering capabilities'.
- Position the Company as a single-source, ultra-precision partner to global OEMs and ride India's emergence as an aerospace manufacturing and localisation hub as OEMs diversify their supply chains.
- Convert defence self-reliance policy into work: exclusive partner to the L&T-BEL consortium on the 5th-Generation AMCA programme, and expectation that customs duty exemptions and higher defence allocations are a tailwind for domestic manufacturing expansion.
- Build an IP-led unmanned systems business through the incubated Dynauton Systems, spanning loitering munitions (Kaatil), surveillance UAS (Kavaa), VTOL ISR (Cheel), tethered UAS (Patang) and a counter-drone portfolio, with serial manufacturing rather than assembly.
- Indigenise critical UAS subsystems - proprietary autopilot, Ground Vehicle Processing Unit, Battery Management System, Power Distribution Unit and Ground Control Station software - to move design, firmware and production in-house and cut dependence on imported components.
- Add new OEM work packages up the value chain: Dassault Falcon 6X complete rear fuselage (Section 5), Deutsche Aircraft D328eco rear fuselage assembly line, and next-generation aerospace composites via a Memorandum of Agreement with Hutchinson.
- Differentiate on manufacturing and industrialisation sophistication - the Company claims a historic industry first in launching AI-enabled First Article Inspection for the Airbus A220 Aft Service Door, 'marking us as the first aerostructure manufacturer globally to integrate Artificial Intelligence directly into the industrialisation process'.
- Consolidate Hydraulics manufacturing in Bangalore and shrink the UK footprint: the Swindon restructuring begun in September 2025 plus transfer of manufacturing activities and capacity from the UK to India, explicitly to rationalise capital employment.
- Grow the Hydraulics aftermarket and industrial channels alongside OEM sales to improve resilience, margin profile and capital efficiency, while investing in advanced capabilities and automation.
- Pivot the Metallurgy business (Eisenwerk Erla) away from European automotive dependence toward defence and specialised engineering, with aerospace castings and forgings held out only as a conditional longer-term option under strict capital discipline.
- Run the business for capital efficiency rather than volume: management names 'disciplined programme ramp-up and long-term execution excellence as the keys to enhancing competitiveness, margins and return on capital employed', and frames the UK-to-Bangalore reorganisation as creating a leaner operating model 'while rationalising capital employment'.
- Treat programme execution and quality culture as the moat - years of industrialisation, compliance verification and process stabilisation, sustained investment in technical training, systems-engineering discipline and talent retention to absorb complex technology transfers and ramp output at zero-defect quality.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body:
Expansion in FY26 is programme-led rather than greenfield-plant-led, and it is concentrated at Dynamatic Aerotropolis in Bangalore. The Board's Report states that 'During the year under review, the Group incurred capital expenditure of Rs. 5,998 lakhs for physical infrastructure and Rs. 2,464 lakhs for procurement and development of intangible assets', The Board adds that 'Significant investments have been made in plant and machinery, building, data security, information systems, design and development activities, for the future benefits of the Group'.

AEROSPACE. The defining physical build-out of the year was the industrialisation of the Airbus A220 door line at Bangalore: the Company reports 'the successful industrialisation and delivery readiness of the first complete ship-set of all eight Airbus A220 doors from our Bangalore facility - completed ahead of schedule', covering passenger, service, cargo and over-wing emergency exit doors. Alongside it, Dynamatic launched AI-enabled First Article Inspection for the A220 Aft Service Door, claiming to be 'the first aerostructure manufacturer globally to integrate Artificial Intelligence directly into the industrialisation process'.

Two new OEM work packages add capacity requirement. A strategic agreement with Dassault Aviation covers manufacture and assembly of 'the complete rear fuselage (Section 5)' for the Falcon 6X, building on the already-delivered rear fuel tank assembly. For Deutsche Aircraft, the 'Rear Fuselage Assembly Jigs and the assembly line for the 40-seater D328eco regional turboprop are nearing completion at Dynamatic Aerotropolis' - a tooling and line installation with no stated commissioning date. A Memorandum of Agreement with Hutchinson is intended 'to expand our capabilities across next-generation aerospace composites for commercial and defence platforms', i.e. a capability rather than a tonnage addition.

SUBSIDIARY RAMP. Dynamatic Manufacturing Limited, two years after commencing operations, 'has scaled to manufacture over 250,000 detail parts annually' supporting Airbus, Dassault, Bell Textron and other global partners, and during the year additionally 'started its operations into the Hydraulics business and commenced the manufacturing and supply of hydraulic pumps' - a second product line inside an existing site. The order book is described as positive and 'in process of expanding steadily'.

DEFENCE / UAV. Dynamatic reports being selected as the exclusive partner for the L&T-BEL consortium's 5th-Generation Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) project. Separately, Dynauton Limited was incorporated on 10th April 2026 (i.e. after the balance-sheet date) as a wholly owned subsidiary 'with the objective of designing and manufacturing advanced Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and critical subsystems, including gimbals, autopilots, radars, propulsion units, avionics, and software solutions'; the Board says the Group is 'well advanced in the development of Dynauton, the UAV internal startup it has recently incorporated, and its purely indigenous technological capabilities, product line and industrial capacity'. Management expects 'customs duty exemptions and increased defence allocations' to be a tailwind for domestic manufacturing expansion.

HYDRAULICS. Indian operations were able to 'expand capacity and achieve higher volume deliveries of hydraulic pumps', and the Company says it is 'making significant investments in advanced capabilities and automation to meet evolving customer requirements and support sustainable growth'. No rupee quantum or capacity figure is attached.

CONTRACTION / RELOCATION. The offsetting move is a reduction of UK footprint rather than an addition: 'In September 2025, UK management initiated a comprehensive restructuring program at our Swindon facility to streamline the product portfolio and optimize the workforce', and the Group 'completed the transfer of relevant manufacturing activities and capacity and reorganisation of manufacturing to Bangalore'. This is stated to be intended 'to create a leaner and more competitive operating model, enhancing throughput, delivery responsiveness and operational agility, while rationalising capital employment'. In Metallurgy, Eisenwerk Erla 'is currently transitioning from an automotive and foundry focus to the aerospace and defence sector', and the Company says only that 'Longer term, it may consider capabilities in aerospace castings, forgings and specialised engineering' - explicitly conditional, and 'with a strong focus on capital employment'.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Global Aerospace and Defence demand is stated to remain robust, supporting sustained segment growth and long-term programme visibility.
- As OEMs diversify and deepen global supply chains, India is becoming an increasingly important aerospace manufacturing and localisation hub, with the Group positioned as a beneficiary.
- Stable volume growth across the Airbus A320 family and A330 programmes, aided by a normalising global supply chain that significantly improved delivery timelines; Boeing P-8 and F-15 continued at a steady pace.
- Airbus is described as planning to deliver over 1,000 aircraft to Indian carriers in the coming years, framed as demand pull for the collaborative footprint.
- Ongoing customer programmes and new strategic partnerships are expected to support long-term business visibility and growth.
- Aerospace margin normalisation is flagged: revenue momentum remains robust but profitability was broadly stable and grew only moderately, attributed to growth investments and project mix.
- Hydraulics demand is driven by rising farm mechanisation, infrastructure-led economic development and supportive government policies for agricultural and construction equipment; demand for agricultural tractors is described as at an all-time high and domestic demand resilient across OEM, industrial and aftermarket channels.
- Hydraulics margins are expected to improve gradually on stable domestic demand, with UK restructuring initiatives expected to aid margin recovery over the medium term.
- UK Hydraulics is a drag: revenue declined on reduced OEM demand and planned operational rationalisation, with rationalisation measures said to have temporarily impacted near-term profitability.

risks.note: The Board's Report says 'The Metallurgy segment continues to operate in a difficult European environment, impacted by weakness in the German automotive sector, elevated energy costs and broader geopolitical uncertainty', and that management states 'increased exposure to defence is necessary to reduce dependence on the weaker automotive industry and support future profitable growth' - i.e. the current customer base is itself the risk, and the pivot to defence and specialised engineering is unproven.
risks.risk: Structural weakness in the German/European automotive end-market that the Metallurgy business depends on

risks.note: Elevated energy costs are named as a driver of the Metallurgy segment's difficulty alongside German automotive weakness and geopolitical uncertainty. Foundry and machining economics are energy-intensive, and the stated response is limited to 'very strict cost discipline, operational efficiency measures and a strategic shift toward higher-value applications', which does not remove the input-cost exposure.
risks.risk: Elevated energy costs and European cost competitiveness at the Eisenwerk Erla foundry

risks.note: UK Hydraulics revenue 'declined 25.5% due to product rationalisation and ongoing restructuring initiatives' and 'reduced OEM demand'. The Group states 'the returns from coordination and integrated operations between the Indian and UK operations having substantially diminished' and has completed a transfer of manufacturing capacity to Bangalore. The margin recovery is stated only as an expectation 'over the medium term', so revenue has already been lost while the benefit is still pending.
risks.risk: Execution risk on the UK restructuring and the transfer of manufacturing to Bangalore

risks.note: Aerospace 'continued to be the primary growth driver' and growth is 'underpinned by long-term programmes with major OEMs including Airbus, Boeing, Bell Textron, Dassault Aviation and Deutsche Aircraft'. Segment revenue is therefore tied to a handful of OEM build rates and programme decisions the Company does not control, and the same OEM set also underwrites the 'new strategic partnerships' management says will support long-term visibility.
risks.risk: Concentration on a small number of large global aerospace OEM programmes

risks.note: The Board's Report notes that while 'revenue momentum remains robust, profitability was broadly stable and grew moderately during the year, indicating some margin normalization amid growth investments and project mix'. The company itself identifies 'disciplined programme ramp-up and long-term execution excellence as the keys to enhancing competitiveness, margins and return on capital employed' — an admission that a mis-managed ramp erodes returns.
risks.risk: Margin dilution from aerospace programme ramp-up and growth investment

risks.note: Explicitly flagged for the near term: 'Near-term performance will remain influenced by raw material availability, commodity input costs, and financing conditions for end customers.' The last of these adds a credit-cycle dependency on top of the Company's own input-cost exposure.
risks.risk: Raw material availability, commodity input costs and customer financing conditions

risks.note: Named a Risk in the BRSR material-issues table with negative financial implications: 'Inadequate safeguards may lead to data breaches, loss of stakeholder trust, and compliance issues.' Material for a defence and aerospace supplier handling OEM-controlled technical data; mitigation is an ISO 27001-aligned information security management system with risk assessments, firewalls, intrusion detection and endpoint protection.
risks.risk: Data privacy and cyber security across operations and the supply chain

risks.note: Two BRSR material issues rated Risk with negative implications. Failure to control workplace hazards 'can lead to accidents, regulatory non-compliance, and reputational damage', and labour-rights lapses 'may lead to legal penalties, reputational damage, lower ESG ratings and operational disruptions'. Heightened because the Company operates 'in sectors like aerospace and automotive manufacturing, where labour standards and safety are critical', and the stated risk explicitly extends beyond own operations to the 'global supply chain'.
risks.risk: Workplace health, safety, human-rights and labour standards across a global manufacturing footprint

currentContext.expansion:
Expansion in FY26 is programme-led rather than greenfield-plant-led, and it is concentrated at Dynamatic Aerotropolis in Bangalore. The Board's Report states that 'During the year under review, the Group incurred capital expenditure of Rs. 5,998 lakhs for physical infrastructure and Rs. 2,464 lakhs for procurement and development of intangible assets', The Board adds that 'Significant investments have been made in plant and machinery, building, data security, information systems, design and development activities, for the future benefits of the Group'.

AEROSPACE. The defining physical build-out of the year was the industrialisation of the Airbus A220 door line at Bangalore: the Company reports 'the successful industrialisation and delivery readiness of the first complete ship-set of all eight Airbus A220 doors from our Bangalore facility - completed ahead of schedule', covering passenger, service, cargo and over-wing emergency exit doors. Alongside it, Dynamatic launched AI-enabled First Article Inspection for the A220 Aft Service Door, claiming to be 'the first aerostructure manufacturer globally to integrate Artificial Intelligence directly into the industrialisation process'.

Two new OEM work packages add capacity requirement. A strategic agreement with Dassault Aviation covers manufacture and assembly of 'the complete rear fuselage (Section 5)' for the Falcon 6X, building on the already-delivered rear fuel tank assembly. For Deutsche Aircraft, the 'Rear Fuselage Assembly Jigs and the assembly line for the 40-seater D328eco regional turboprop are nearing completion at Dynamatic Aerotropolis' - a tooling and line installation with no stated commissioning date. A Memorandum of Agreement with Hutchinson is intended 'to expand our capabilities across next-generation aerospace composites for commercial and defence platforms', i.e. a capability rather than a tonnage addition.

SUBSIDIARY RAMP. Dynamatic Manufacturing Limited, two years after commencing operations, 'has scaled to manufacture over 250,000 detail parts annually' supporting Airbus, Dassault, Bell Textron and other global partners, and during the year additionally 'started its operations into the Hydraulics business and commenced the manufacturing and supply of hydraulic pumps' - a second product line inside an existing site. The order book is described as positive and 'in process of expanding steadily'.

DEFENCE / UAV. Dynamatic reports being selected as the exclusive partner for the L&T-BEL consortium's 5th-Generation Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) project. Separately, Dynauton Limited was incorporated on 10th April 2026 (i.e. after the balance-sheet date) as a wholly owned subsidiary 'with the objective of designing and manufacturing advanced Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and critical subsystems, including gimbals, autopilots, radars, propulsion units, avionics, and software solutions'; the Board says the Group is 'well advanced in the development of Dynauton, the UAV internal startup it has recently incorporated, and its purely indigenous technological capabilities, product line and industrial capacity'. Management expects 'customs duty exemptions and increased defence allocations' to be a tailwind for domestic manufacturing expansion.

HYDRAULICS. Indian operations were able to 'expand capacity and achieve higher volume deliveries of hydraulic pumps', and the Company says it is 'making significant investments in advanced capabilities and automation to meet evolving customer requirements and support sustainable growth'. No rupee quantum or capacity figure is attached.

CONTRACTION / RELOCATION. The offsetting move is a reduction of UK footprint rather than an addition: 'In September 2025, UK management initiated a comprehensive restructuring program at our Swindon facility to streamline the product portfolio and optimize the workforce', and the Group 'completed the transfer of relevant manufacturing activities and capacity and reorganisation of manufacturing to Bangalore'. This is stated to be intended 'to create a leaner and more competitive operating model, enhancing throughput, delivery responsiveness and operational agility, while rationalising capital employment'. In Metallurgy, Eisenwerk Erla 'is currently transitioning from an automotive and foundry focus to the aerospace and defence sector', and the Company says only that 'Longer term, it may consider capabilities in aerospace castings, forgings and specialised engineering' - explicitly conditional, and 'with a strong focus on capital employment'.

risks.risk: Structural weakness in the German/European automotive end-market that the Metallurgy business depends on
risks.note: The Board's Report says 'The Metallurgy segment continues to operate in a difficult European environment, impacted by weakness in the German automotive sector, elevated energy costs and broader geopolitical uncertainty', and that management states 'increased exposure to defence is necessary to reduce dependence on the weaker automotive industry and support future profitable growth' - i.e. the current customer base is itself the risk, and the pivot to defence and specialised engineering is unproven.

risks.risk: Elevated energy costs and European cost competitiveness at the Eisenwerk Erla foundry
risks.note: Elevated energy costs are named as a driver of the Metallurgy segment's difficulty alongside German automotive weakness and geopolitical uncertainty. Foundry and machining economics are energy-intensive, and the stated response is limited to 'very strict cost discipline, operational efficiency measures and a strategic shift toward higher-value applications', which does not remove the input-cost exposure.

risks.risk: Execution risk on the UK restructuring and the transfer of manufacturing to Bangalore
risks.note: UK Hydraulics revenue 'declined 25.5% due to product rationalisation and ongoing restructuring initiatives' and 'reduced OEM demand'. The Group states 'the returns from coordination and integrated operations between the Indian and UK operations having substantially diminished' and has completed a transfer of manufacturing capacity to Bangalore. The margin recovery is stated only as an expectation 'over the medium term', so revenue has already been lost while the benefit is still pending.

risks.risk: Concentration on a small number of large global aerospace OEM programmes
risks.note: Aerospace 'continued to be the primary growth driver' and growth is 'underpinned by long-term programmes with major OEMs including Airbus, Boeing, Bell Textron, Dassault Aviation and Deutsche Aircraft'. Segment revenue is therefore tied to a handful of OEM build rates and programme decisions the Company does not control, and the same OEM set also underwrites the 'new strategic partnerships' management says will support long-term visibility.

risks.risk: Margin dilution from aerospace programme ramp-up and growth investment
risks.note: The Board's Report notes that while 'revenue momentum remains robust, profitability was broadly stable and grew moderately during the year, indicating some margin normalization amid growth investments and project mix'. The company itself identifies 'disciplined programme ramp-up and long-term execution excellence as the keys to enhancing competitiveness, margins and return on capital employed' — an admission that a mis-managed ramp erodes returns.

risks.risk: Raw material availability, commodity input costs and customer financing conditions
risks.note: Explicitly flagged for the near term: 'Near-term performance will remain influenced by raw material availability, commodity input costs, and financing conditions for end customers.' The last of these adds a credit-cycle dependency on top of the Company's own input-cost exposure.

risks.risk: Data privacy and cyber security across operations and the supply chain
risks.note: Named a Risk in the BRSR material-issues table with negative financial implications: 'Inadequate safeguards may lead to data breaches, loss of stakeholder trust, and compliance issues.' Material for a defence and aerospace supplier handling OEM-controlled technical data; mitigation is an ISO 27001-aligned information security management system with risk assessments, firewalls, intrusion detection and endpoint protection.

risks.risk: Workplace health, safety, human-rights and labour standards across a global manufacturing footprint
risks.note: Two BRSR material issues rated Risk with negative implications. Failure to control workplace hazards 'can lead to accidents, regulatory non-compliance, and reputational damage', and labour-rights lapses 'may lead to legal penalties, reputational damage, lower ESG ratings and operational disruptions'. Heightened because the Company operates 'in sectors like aerospace and automotive manufacturing, where labour standards and safety are critical', and the stated risk explicitly extends beyond own operations to the 'global supply chain'.

risks.risk: Water scarcity and environmental footprint at manufacturing sites
risks.note: BRSR names water management a Risk: 'Water scarcity poses a risk to DTL by potentially disrupting manufacturing operations, Inadequate water management can lead to increased operational costs, regulatory challenges, and reputational concerns.' (punctuation as printed in the report).

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Dynamatic Technologies is a Bangalore-headquartered Tier-I precision engineering group that builds flight-critical airframe structures for global aerospace OEMs and hydraulic gear pumps for off-highway and agricultural equipment, with exports contributing 50.10% of turnover.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Dynamatic Technologies Limited, incorporated in 1973 and listed on the BSE and NSE, describes itself as a manufacturing and engineering services company operating in two disclosed business activities - Aerospace & Defence and Hydraulics - which together account for 100% of turnover, with a third Metallurgy business run through its German subsidiary Eisenwerk Erla. Through Dynamatic-Oldland Aerospace it manufactures flight-critical airframe structures and high-precision Class 1 parts as a Tier-I supplier to Airbus, Boeing, Bell, Deutsche Aircraft, Dassault Aviation, Hutchinson and Thales, and domestically to defence PSUs HAL and BEL; typical work packages are control surfaces (wings, ailerons, wing flaps), fuselages, doors and flap track beams. Through Dynamatic Hydraulics it designs and manufactures gear pumps, motors, valves and complete hydraulic systems in Bangalore and Swindon for agricultural, construction and off-highway OEMs such as Mahindra & Mahindra, John Deere, JCB, TAFE, Cummins, Alexander Dennis, MacDon and ACE, and supplies hydraulic transmission, steering, turret control and brake actuating systems to India's defence forces.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global Aerospace and Defence demand is stated to remain robust, supporting sustained segment growth and long-term programme visibility.
- As OEMs diversify and deepen global supply chains, India is becoming an increasingly important aerospace manufacturing and localisation hub, with the Group positioned as a beneficiary.
- Stable volume growth across the Airbus A320 family and A330 programmes, aided by a normalising global supply chain that significantly improved delivery timelines; Boeing P-8 and F-15 continued at a steady pace.
- Airbus is described as planning to deliver over 1,000 aircraft to Indian carriers in the coming years, framed as demand pull for the collaborative footprint.
- Ongoing customer programmes and new strategic partnerships are expected to support long-term business visibility and growth.
- Aerospace margin normalisation is flagged: revenue momentum remains robust but profitability was broadly stable and grew only moderately, attributed to growth investments and project mix.
- Hydraulics demand is driven by rising farm mechanisation, infrastructure-led economic development and supportive government policies for agricultural and construction equipment; demand for agricultural tractors is described as at an all-time high and domestic demand resilient across OEM, industrial and aftermarket channels.
- Hydraulics margins are expected to improve gradually on stable domestic demand, with UK restructuring initiatives expected to aid margin recovery over the medium term.
- UK Hydraulics is a drag: revenue declined on reduced OEM demand and planned operational rationalisation, with rationalisation measures said to have temporarily impacted near-term profitability.
- Metallurgy faces a cautious European demand environment - weakness in the German automotive sector, elevated energy costs, fierce global competition and geopolitical uncertainty - though gradual demand stabilisation and easing inflation are cited as support.
- A growing German defence budget and new security priorities are named as the opportunity that could support Metallurgy's product diversification and regional industrial stability.
- Near-term Metallurgy performance is said to remain influenced by raw material availability, commodity input costs and financing conditions for end customers.
- Policy tailwinds expected from customs duty exemptions and increased defence allocations for domestic manufacturing expansion.
- 'Key platforms include the Airbus A220, Airbus A330, Dassault Falcon 6X and D328eco, with a strong order book expected to support continued revenue growth in the coming years' - the only forward-looking order-book statement in the annual report, and it carries no value, tenure or book-to-bill.
- Aerospace growth in FY2026 is attributed to 'resilient performance and execution of commercial order books'.
- Dynamatic Manufacturing Limited: 'The order book for the business looks positive and in process of expanding steadily.'
- Programme visibility is described qualitatively only - ongoing customer programmes and new strategic partnerships are expected to support long-term business visibility and growth; no order-book value, tenure or book-to-bill is disclosed anywhere in this bundle.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Hydraulics: 16-17% EBITDA (rising with pricing power); Aerospace: High-margin (>25% EBITDA); German metallurgy: Break-even to positive; Foundry divestment removes Rs 20-25cr annual drag; cost compression achieved via automation and digital thread efficiencies.

capital_allocation.body: Rs 120cr net proceeds from JFTL and wind farm divestments to be used: 60% debt reduction (Rs 200cr dollarized), 40% reinvested in aerospace/hydraulics capex; zero dividend payout policy implied; land sale to govt ensures clean capital return.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body:
Expansion in FY26 is programme-led rather than greenfield-plant-led, and it is concentrated at Dynamatic Aerotropolis in Bangalore. The Board's Report states that 'During the year under review, the Group incurred capital expenditure of Rs. 5,998 lakhs for physical infrastructure and Rs. 2,464 lakhs for procurement and development of intangible assets', The Board adds that 'Significant investments have been made in plant and machinery, building, data security, information systems, design and development activities, for the future benefits of the Group'.

AEROSPACE. The defining physical build-out of the year was the industrialisation of the Airbus A220 door line at Bangalore: the Company reports 'the successful industrialisation and delivery readiness of the first complete ship-set of all eight Airbus A220 doors from our Bangalore facility - completed ahead of schedule', covering passenger, service, cargo and over-wing emergency exit doors. Alongside it, Dynamatic launched AI-enabled First Article Inspection for the A220 Aft Service Door, claiming to be 'the first aerostructure manufacturer globally to integrate Artificial Intelligence directly into the industrialisation process'.

Two new OEM work packages add capacity requirement. A strategic agreement with Dassault Aviation covers manufacture and assembly of 'the complete rear fuselage (Section 5)' for the Falcon 6X, building on the already-delivered rear fuel tank assembly. For Deutsche Aircraft, the 'Rear Fuselage Assembly Jigs and the assembly line for the 40-seater D328eco regional turboprop are nearing completion at Dynamatic Aerotropolis' - a tooling and line installation with no stated commissioning date. A Memorandum of Agreement with Hutchinson is intended 'to expand our capabilities across next-generation aerospace composites for commercial and defence platforms', i.e. a capability rather than a tonnage addition.

SUBSIDIARY RAMP. Dynamatic Manufacturing Limited, two years after commencing operations, 'has scaled to manufacture over 250,000 detail parts annually' supporting Airbus, Dassault, Bell Textron and other global partners, and during the year additionally 'started its operations into the Hydraulics business and commenced the manufacturing and supply of hydraulic pumps' - a second product line inside an existing site. The order book is described as positive and 'in process of expanding steadily'.

DEFENCE / UAV. Dynamatic reports being selected as the exclusive partner for the L&T-BEL consortium's 5th-Generation Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) project. Separately, Dynauton Limited was incorporated on 10th April 2026 (i.e. after the balance-sheet date) as a wholly owned subsidiary 'with the objective of designing and manufacturing advanced Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and critical subsystems, including gimbals, autopilots, radars, propulsion units, avionics, and software solutions'; the Board says the Group is 'well advanced in the development of Dynauton, the UAV internal startup it has recently incorporated, and its purely indigenous technological capabilities, product line and industrial capacity'. Management expects 'customs duty exemptions and increased defence allocations' to be a tailwind for domestic manufacturing expansion.

HYDRAULICS. Indian operations were able to 'expand capacity and achieve higher volume deliveries of hydraulic pumps', and the Company says it is 'making significant investments in advanced capabilities and automation to meet evolving customer requirements and support sustainable growth'. No rupee quantum or capacity figure is attached.

CONTRACTION / RELOCATION. The offsetting move is a reduction of UK footprint rather than an addition: 'In September 2025, UK management initiated a comprehensive restructuring program at our Swindon facility to streamline the product portfolio and optimize the workforce', and the Group 'completed the transfer of relevant manufacturing activities and capacity and reorganisation of manufacturing to Bangalore'. This is stated to be intended 'to create a leaner and more competitive operating model, enhancing throughput, delivery responsiveness and operational agility, while rationalising capital employment'. In Metallurgy, Eisenwerk Erla 'is currently transitioning from an automotive and foundry focus to the aerospace and defence sector', and the Company says only that 'Longer term, it may consider capabilities in aerospace castings, forgings and specialised engineering' - explicitly conditional, and 'with a strong focus on capital employment'.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Highly confident, optimistic, and strategic; emphasized pricing power, operational excellence, and long-term moats; transparent about past failures (foundry) and current wins; tone reflects leadership in indigenization narrative; proactive on COVID resilience and biosecurity.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Dominant share in Indian tractor hydraulics: the Company states it has achieved and sustained over 80% market share for pumps on agricultural tractors produced in India and a 38% share of agricultural tractors produced globally.
- Scale in gear pumps - described as one of the world's largest manufacturers of hydraulic gear pumps and valves, with three Bangalore plants producing nearly one million pumps a year and over 50 years (six decades in the UK) of gear pump design experience.
- Tier-I qualification on flight-critical aerostructures for Airbus, Boeing, Bell, Deutsche Aircraft, Dassault Aviation, Hutchinson and Thales - approvals that take years of industrialisation, compliance verification and process stabilisation and are therefore high switching cost for the OEM.
- Demonstrated execution credibility: the industrialisation of all eight Airbus A220 doors was completed ahead of schedule, and the Airbus SE Board held its first-ever India meeting at the Company's facility.
- Process differentiation - the Company states it is one of the first companies globally in aerospace to adopt Advanced Product Quality Planning and the Production Part Approval Process, cross-deployed from its automotive business, and says this has been appreciated by all the major OEMs including Boeing, Airbus, Bell, Deutsche Aircraft, Dassault Aviation Group, Hutchinson Group and Thales.
- Owned intellectual property: the Company owns the IP rights of the pumps it designs, with the entire design and development process managed on the Windchill platform and engineering data protected in digital form.
- Manufacturing depth - automated robotic machining, five-axis components in aluminium, steel and titanium, in-house tooling, in-house sealed-quench gear heat treatment, and attached metallurgy, metrology, validation and endurance testing laboratories.
- Vertically supported R&D - JKM Research Farm Limited acts as the R&D facilitator for design concept, functional prototype testing and technical information, and the Company cites rapid prototyping offering the lowest time to market for the fluid power industry.
- Privileged access to India's next-generation defence programmes as exclusive partner to the L&T-BEL consortium on the AMCA, plus a domestic UAS product line built in-house.
- Captive green energy sources at its facilities, and an extensive marketing network with sales and servicing branches in key cities worldwide.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Defense order timing delays; commercial aviation recovery slower than expected; geopolitical supply chain disruptions; regulatory delays in SIPCOT NOC for JFTL sale; currency volatility on dollarized debt (mitigated by 50% export coverage); reliance on few global OEMs.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Dynamatic's UK plant captures 90%+ scrap metal value from aerospace machining by re-selling to mills — creating hidden margin; internal RTPCR testing and biosecure certification created unique customer trust during pandemic; 30-year legacy with DRDO/HAL gives unparalleled access to defense R&D pipeline.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Make Aerospace & Defence the centre of gravity of the Group - the Chairman calls it 'the primary engine of Dynamatic's revenues and profitability throughout FY 2025-26, consistently delivering superior margins' - by 'scaling complex aerostructure programs, deepening relationships with global OEMs and strengthening advanced manufacturing and engineering capabilities'.
- Position the Company as a single-source, ultra-precision partner to global OEMs and ride India's emergence as an aerospace manufacturing and localisation hub as OEMs diversify their supply chains.
- Convert defence self-reliance …
